note: Curated Hyrox Asia news. Items land here only when Dina taps Publish on the Coach's desk; edit or delete rows freely. Newest first. Items dated in the future auto-publish on their date — the feed rolls weekly through the season without anyone touching it.

items.title: That's a wrap on 2026 — the season resets
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur closed the Asia-Pacific season on 13 December. From here the story turns to 2027: Hong Kong in January, Bangkok in February, and the big one — Jakarta's second edition.
items.take: Musim pertama selesai. Now we build for the home race — this time with a crowd that knows what Hyrox is.

items.title: KL race week: the last start line of 2026
items.summary: AirAsia HYROX Kuala Lumpur opens Thursday at MITEC — four race days, and the biggest Indonesian travelling contingent of the season is expected.
items.take: Two hours from home, same language. If you're racing — gaspol. If you're watching — the results board updates after.

items.title: Singapore race week: the Little Red Dot calls
items.summary: AIA HYROX Singapore runs 26–29 November at Singapore EXPO — three-plus days of racing, and the closest thing to a second home race for Jakarta athletes.
items.take: Under two hours, no jet lag, air-con venue. The smart second race — and the hawker centres are carb-loading on easy mode.

items.title: Seoul race week: cold air, fast times
items.summary: HYROX Seoul runs 13–15 November at KINTEX — the season's cool-weather race. November in Goyang runs 0–10 °C, which is exactly why PBs go there to happen.
items.take: Cold air means faster splits — but pack a proper jacket, the post-race chill is real. Kram di Seoul hits different.

items.title: Shanghai race week: the Big Dumpling races
items.summary: HYROX Shanghai runs this weekend — the biggest of China's stops this season and a long-haul trip for anyone flying from Jakarta.
items.take: Far for a weekend race, but if you're doing a China double this is the anchor. Watching from the results board this time.

items.title: The November–December block: three races in seven weeks
items.summary: Seoul (13–15 Nov), Singapore (26–29 Nov), Kuala Lumpur (10–13 Dec) — the densest stretch of the APAC calendar. One taper can cover two of them if you plan it right.
items.take: Pick an A-race and a B-race, don't try to peak three times. That's what the 12-week block is for — tanya aja.

items.title: Ten weeks to KL — the window is open
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur on 10 December is ten weeks out — exactly one race-prep block. For first-timers, it's also the friendliest away race on the calendar: two hours, Bahasa works, cheap flights.
items.take: Start this week and you land race-ready with days to spare. Start next month and you're cramming — pilih yang mana?

items.title: Mumbai weekend: the full Indonesian picture
items.summary: Beyond the new Pro Doubles record, Mumbai confirmed the pattern of this season — Indonesian athletes are travelling, entering more divisions, and finishing near the front.
items.take: Last year we were the new kids. Now people check the INA flag in the start list. Beda banget rasanya.

items.title: Indonesian doubles record falls in Mumbai
items.summary: Standy Tjandra and Stephen Kusuma ran 57:43 in Pro Doubles at HYROX Mumbai — a new Indonesian record, three months after taking the Open record on home soil in Jakarta.
items.take: Dua cowok Indo ngangkat bendera di Mumbai. The bar keeps moving — bagus, we like chasing.

items.title: Kuala Lumpur confirmed for December — Malaysia's first HYROX
items.summary: AirAsia HYROX Kuala Lumpur runs 10–13 December at MITEC. Four race days, the closest away race from Jakarta, in a language you already speak.
items.take: Two hours, same language, cheap flights. No excuses left — who's in?

items.title: Seoul and Singapore go back-to-back in November
items.summary: HYROX Seoul runs 13–15 November and AIA HYROX Singapore 26–29 November — two race weekends a fortnight apart, or one very greedy November.
items.take: Cold Seoul air for the PB hunters, then home-region heat in Singapore. Pick one. Or pack for both.

items.title: Gladys Fabiola Christanto sets Indonesian women's Open record in Bangkok
items.summary: 1:08:35 at HYROX Bangkok — the fastest Indonesian women's Open time on record. She also holds the Mixed Doubles record with Timothy Tjahja from Hong Kong in May.
items.take: Perempuan Indo makin cepat. The depth is coming — that's the exciting part.

items.title: Jakarta's debut weekend: eight national records on home soil
items.summary: Indonesia's first HYROX at NICE drew one of the biggest Asia-Pacific fields of the season — and home athletes banked national records across Pro, Open, Doubles and Relay divisions.
items.take: Home crowd did that. Wait till next year.
